added.title: Why is scheduling disabled, and how would you add it safely?
added.answer: The current prototype provides invitation-based consultations, not an implemented appointment service. The selected next step is doctor-booked appointments: separate opaque appointment records, timezone-aware start/end times, ownership checks, transactional overlap prevention and booked/cancelled states. Booking must never bypass invitation admission, begin transcription or create clinical evidence. Patient self-booking, reminders and calendar sync are outside that first release. HL7 FHIR's separate Appointment and Encounter resources provide a design precedent, not evidence that we implement FHIR interoperability. Until the new feature is built and tested, defend it as future work and do not attribute it to the original study respondents.

added.title: Why must the platform super administrator use a separate doctor account?
added.answer: Separation of duties: the configured platform owner manages staff access, not consultations. The server denies clinical permissions to that verified owner even if historical doctor/admin claims remain, and the interface hides clinical links. A separate clinician identity must be explicitly provisioned. Changing the server configuration requires a new deployment. This does not retroactively revoke already-issued media credentials or erase historical records; direct Firestore ownership rules remain a separate migration boundary, not a claim of universal instant revocation.

added.title: Are summaries really deleted after 30 days, and which cron does that?
added.answer: The Firebase autoDeleteSummaries function runs daily but destructive cleanup is opt-in through RETENTION_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED=true. Its configurable cutoff defaults to 30 days; one run deletes at most 400 call-summaries documents and their scheduled-deletions entries. Sessions and any other transcript/chat/summary copies are not a complete purge. The Vercel daily /api/summary/process-queue cron retries summary work; it is not the deletion job. Deployment, enabled policy and successful runs must be verified separately. Age alone is not a deletion receipt, so the UI must not claim confirmed permanent deletion from age alone.

added.title: Can you reuse that scheduled worker for future attachment retention?
added.answer: Reuse the bounded scheduled-worker pattern, not the existing summary query unchanged. Attachment cleanup would need an approved per-object expiry policy, ready/failed/uploading states, storage-object plus metadata deletion, legal-hold rules if required, idempotent retries and reconciliation for partial failure. Never log file content or download tokens. Test dry-run, expiry boundaries, duplicate invocations and orphan cleanup before enabling it. Attachments are disabled today; this is a future plan, not an implemented automatic attachment purge.

added.title: Why can one invitation have multiple history rows, and should history wait for revocation?
added.answer: An invitation is a reusable access policy; an encounter is a specific room opening with its own session id. Leaving and rejoining can create separate completed encounters, including doctor-only openings. Revocation closes future invitation access; it is not the sole encounter-completion event. Active encounters should say Not finalized rather than Awaiting summary, and summary generation must require finalization. Keep distinct records instead of merging by reused room name. A no-patient record is nonclinical, not an AI diagnosis or proof a scheduled patient failed to attend.

added.title: Why is transcription consent asked again when the doctor rejoins?
added.answer: Consent is encounter-scoped and optional. A new room-page mount begins unchecked; a new encounter must not inherit consent merely because it reused a room name or invitation. Device preflight is also intentional because device availability may have changed. This is a privacy-preserving default, not proof of a broken video route. The call works without transcription. A future same-encounter resume could restore a clearly visible choice only with exact session/participant binding and revocation handling; do not silently restart recording.

added.title: Does responsive layout mean the app is proven on every phone and iPad?
added.answer: No. Responsive layout adapts forms, navigation and call controls to narrow and tablet viewports. Compact call layouts use on-demand panels rather than fixed sidebars over the video; wider layouts reserve panel space. Report tested viewport dimensions and browser from the current evidence. Synthetic browser sizing is not an actual iPad/Safari audio-video acceptance test. Confirm real device permissions, keyboard operation, orientation changes, network recovery and optional speech support before claiming device compatibility.

added.title: What belongs in the consultation room rather than repeating invitation management?
added.answer: Show operational context: room/session identity, waiting occupancy versus its configured cap, verified direct-entry audience count, and participant state. Put captured arrival/admission/departure times and identity provenance in expandable details. Never label self-declared email verified or admission as confirmed media attendance. Teams and Zoom use participant/lobby controls separate from richer attendance reports; that is a useful design precedent, not proof of our app's usability. Hashed invitation emails cannot be recovered for display; show recorded participant identities truthfully and manage the invitation separately.

added.title: Does the doctor count as a verified patient visit?
added.answer: No. Creating an invitation, appearing in the direct-entry audience configuration and joining as its owning doctor are not patient visits. Patient counters must be based on reserved patient visits, not the host's presence. Verified-account visits and guests describe identity provenance, not unique people or completed consultations. Reconnects reuse the same active visit. Older invitations may only have a historical aggregate join count; do not invent a verified/guest breakdown for them.

added.title: Why did administrator sign-in open the doctor's Invitations page?
added.answer: The old /admin entry linked to doctor login, and both doctor-login methods always navigated to Invitations. That was a routing defect, not evidence that authentication had granted administration. Dedicated /admin/login and /admin/signup now preserve administrator intent; the server access projection sends authorized administrators to /admin. Doctor login also checks for administrator access before the doctor workflow. Demonstrate the result with synthetic pre-provisioned accounts; screenshots alone do not prove current claims.

added.title: Does the new administrator signup let anyone become an administrator?
added.answer: No. It creates a Firebase Authentication identity only, without writing a privileged profile or custom claim. Google can establish that identity too. The platform owner separately grants Administrator within a clinic. An unapproved identity receives pending-access guidance and can refresh after approval. Never use a client-selected role or signup URL as authority. Demonstrate an unapproved identity being denied by the admin API as well as the page.

added.title: I clicked Grant role, but the account still opens the doctor workspace. Why?
added.answer: Check the selected role and the confirmed result. Doctor grants clinician access only; Administrator adds clinic administration and is restricted to the platform owner. A successful Doctor grant is not a failed Administrator grant. After the correct authorized grant, refresh the recipient's ID token with the Check access again refresh icon (in the Signed in as … bar) or sign in again. Do not silently promote a real account just to make the demonstration look right.

added.title: Why did the configured super administrator appear as a legacy doctor?
added.answer: Bootstrap authority and clinical profile history are different facts. The old list displayed only whether doctor custom claims matched a profile. The server now derives a verified configured owner's effective administration level from Firebase identity plus server-only configuration and labels it Server bootstrap. It does not rewrite that person's historical clinical role or expose the environment allowlist to browsers. An ordinary profile that merely contains the owner's email cannot acquire bootstrap authority.

added.title: What do you do when newly granted access does not appear, or the account service is down?
added.answer: Refresh the recipient's token and re-query the server access projection; granted claims are not automatically present in an already-issued token. Keep a visible checking, pending or retry state. An Auth lookup outage must not be labeled as a deleted account, and an unsuccessful request must not be shown as an empty account list. No client retry grants a role. Existing-token revocation limits remain separate.

added.title: Can patients speak Filipino, Tagalog or Taglish, and what language is the summary?
added.answer: The clinician's browser speech-note selector includes fil-PH and en-US; the selected value is passed to browser recognition. Recognition availability and quality depend on the browser/provider and environment. The current summary prompt requests English output and preservation of uncertain names, medicines, measurements and short clinical phrases. A language selector is not a validated Tagalog speech or translation accuracy result. We have not measured Tagalog/Taglish error rates or clinical translation safety.

added.title: How would you validate bilingual AI summaries rather than just demonstrate them?
added.answer: Use synthetic or explicitly consented paired Filipino/English scripts reviewed by a qualified clinician and bilingual reviewer. Compare source speech, captured text and generated draft separately. Record recognition errors, omissions, unsupported facts and translation changes to negation, dose, duration and names; assess reviewer agreement and report failures. A few correct examples do not establish accuracy. The current study's acceptability survey is not that experiment, and the clinician must verify the draft.
